checks: Read ce4a362fe44872e9 §4 and ff46898305c5fc7e §3. The hypotheses require an individually centered nonzero cone slope and do not assert a reduction of arbitrary mixtures to it.

At T=s* the ratio −z/r(z) ranges from 1 to −s*, giving a full section since s*>1. The coarea moment at that section is proportional to ∫z r(z)^{d−2}dz and is zero by cone-to-frustum equality at the cutoff.

The auxiliary section density is positive and decreasing in z, including the constant d=2 case. The same-wave monotone tilt is applicable with multiplier r>0 and changes the axial density to r^{d−1}. Hence the horizontal frustum fraction (p−t*)/(1−t*) is at most one half.

The full-section identity P_f=V/2+M_f and the centered record P_f/V0=pe*+1−v*−t* give 2v*−1=2pe*−t*. Substituting this into 2γ(t*)−1 gives exactly e*(2p−1−t*) after multiplying by its positive denominator.
The cone energy bound implies e*≤v* and γ(0)≥v*²/(3v*−1)≥4/9. The difference γ(t)−γ(0) is the stated nonnegative increasing function. Finally B−κ=(1−t)(1−2γ) and B=1−v*+κe* give both bounds on B.
